claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 can be homogenized as a single-phase high-temperature BCC alloy by holding it at 900°C in an inert atmosphere.
Phase stability in high-temperature BCC Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is governed by a thermodynamically driven, Al-induced short-range-ordering process.
Al-induced short-range order nucleates an ordered B2 phase.
Cooling rate from the high-temperature state strongly controls the atomic diffusion required for local ordering.
The structural mediator is local redistribution of Al atoms within the BCC matrix, producing short-range order and eventual B2 nucleation.
Al substitution in the Cr-Co-Fe-Ni BCC lattice creates local lattice distortions.
The Al-induced lattice distortions favor a lower-free-energy ordered configuration.
Slow cooling provides sufficient atomic mobility for Al atoms to cluster and establish short-range order.
Al-rich short-range-ordered regions act as nuclei for the B2 phase.
Rapid quenching suppresses diffusion and retains the disordered BCC structure.
Slow-cooled samples will contain more B2 phase than rapidly quenched samples.
B2 formation in slow-cooled samples will produce split or new XRD peaks.
Ordered regions associated with B2 formation will be observable by TEM in slow-cooled samples.
DSC of slow-cooled samples will show exothermic peaks corresponding to the ordering reaction.
Rapidly quenched samples will mainly retain the high-temperature disordered BCC structure.
Rapid quenching from 900°C produces a baseline having a single disordered BCC phase with no detectable ordered regions.
The proposed ordering mechanism operates when thermal treatment permits diffusion between approximately 750°C and 900°C.
The proposed mechanism is specifically applicable to Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
Composition changes or thermal treatments substantially outside the stated range may alter ordering kinetics and the thermodynamic driving force.
